summary: Peter von Bradke was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the Imperial University of Dorpat, University of Tübingen, Leipzig University, and University of Giessen, studying under Rudolf von Roth and Leo Meyer. He held a post at Giessen from 1886 to 1896.
Petra Kieffer-Pülz is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. A pupil of Heinz Bechert, she served as a Research Fellow at the Academy of Sciences and Literature Mainz (attested 2013-2016).

Petra Maurer is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She held posts at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.
Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She completed her MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Maha Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull.

Phanit Jetjiravat specializes in Buddhist studies, earning a Master of Arts in the field at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the academic advisement of Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn was a sinologist and historian who studied at Harvard, SOAS, and Georgetown. He served at the University of Chicago (1963-1978), Harvard University from 1978, and directed the Fairbank Center for Chinese Studies (1980-1986).

Philip A. Mellor is a religious studies scholar who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester by 1989. He served as Professor of Religion and Social Theory and Head of the School of Humanities at the University of Leeds.

Philip B. Yampolsky was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology who studied under Yoshitaka Iriya. He served at Columbia University as East Asian Library librarian and Japanese lecturer, and chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.
Philip Deslippe is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. Attested in 2020, he earned his PhD and served as a teaching associate at the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Philip L. Quinn was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He held academic posts at Brown University (~1969-1985) and the University of Notre Dame (~1985-2004).

Philip Whalen was an author and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Reed College and under Richard Baker. He served as visiting poet at Naropa University, resident teacher at South Ridge Zendo, and abbot of Hartford Street Zen Center.

Philipp A. Maas is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Bonn under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler. He held posts at Bonn, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, University of Vienna, and Leipzig University.

Philippe Turenne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori, also studying under Richard P. Hayes, Khenpo Palden Sherab, and other traditional Tibetan scholars.

Philippe-Édouard Foucaux was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He served as Professor of Tibetan at INALCO from 1854 and Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France from 1857 to 1894.

Phillip B. Zarrilli was a scholar of Indology and related fields. He held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from approximately 1979 to 1998 and at the University of Exeter from approximately 1998 to 2020.
Phillip E. Bloom is a scholar of Sinology, art history, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under the doctoral supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

Phra Brahmagunabhorn is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University. He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phra Brahmapundit is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997-2018) and held leadership roles with the International Council for the Day of Vesak and International Association of Buddhist Universities.

Phra Kiattisak Ponampon is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned an MA at the University of Otago under Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie. In 2013, he also studied under scholars including Jinhua Chen and Seishi Karashima.

Phra Sigambhirayan is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Bachelor of Liberal Arts at Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an M.A. in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.
